families.valid_parameter_predicate: template default n=2; the added poison INVARIANTS clause is `&&[0<=i<n]( &&[i<j<n] (r[i] && X r[j] -> F(g[i] && g[j])) )`, which is a vacuously true empty conjunction for n=1 -- meaning n=1 would NOT be a valid instantiation of the intended unrealizable obstruction (it would likely be realizable, same as the base round_robin_arbiter). Valid range for this family's intended obstruction is therefore n>=2, not n>=1 as the bare template comment would suggest; not yet independently confirmed by an actual n=1 solve.

families.status: selected and justified from the actual template. Confirmed by direct code reading (not assumed from the handoff's caution alone) that Acacia's -s never exports a controller for an unreal-arm win: src/arg_parser.hh strips extra real arms when -s is given but keeps all unreal arms in the portfolio, and src/solver/solver_invoker.cc:715 asserts synth_fname and check_unreal are mutually exclusive on the main solve path. Traced the exact transformation Acacia's own UNREAL_X_FORMULA worker applies internally (solver_invoker.cc ~1090-1095 and ~421-433): swap input_aps<->output_aps, then wrap every atom that was an ORIGINAL output in X() (the move-order correction plan section 6.3 warns about), and do NOT negate the objective (only the REAL worker negates). A TLSF-level adapter (swap INPUTS/OUTPUTS declarations, X-shift the former-output atoms, feed the unnegated original guarantee to Acacia's ordinary -s synthesis with no -u flag at all) is the concrete next step this traces out -- but it was not implemented or run this session: getting the swap/shift/negation combination even slightly wrong produces an UNSOUND witness that 'verifies' by construction, and the plan is explicit that this needs differential testing against explicit tiny games before trusting it on a family, which is real, separate work, not a one-line follow-on. Deferred deliberately, not abandoned -- the mechanism is now fully characterized, not just flagged as hard.
